lunch.name: Kare-Kare (Philippine Peanut Stew)
lunch.description: Filipino national dish - peanut stew with beef and vegetables. Blend of Spanish and Chinese influences with indigenous ingredients
ingredients: 500g mixed vegetables (eggplant, bok choy, string beans)
instructions: Boil beef with salt until tender (45 min-1 hour)
Heat annatto oil, sauté garlic and onion
Sprinkle flour, stir until golden
Add peanut butter and beef broth, mix well
Add cooked beef and vegetables, simmer 15-20 minutes
Season with salt, pepper and shrimp paste
Serve over rice with shrimp paste on side
lunch.notes: Annatto oil gives distinctive color and flavor. Shrimp paste (bagoong) is essential seasoning
lunch.fun_fact: Kare-Kare is Filipino national dish, blend of Spanish and Chinese influences with indigenous ingredients. Most popular fiesta dish
alternatives: Adjust peanut butter amount for creaminess

dinner.name: Lumpia (Filipino Spring Rolls)
dinner.description: Crispy fried spring rolls filled with pork and vegetables - Filipino appetizer dinner
ingredients: For dipping: sweet and sour sauce or vinegar with garlic
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in large wok or skillet over high heat
Add minced garlic, cook 30 seconds until fragrant
Add ground pork, breaking it apart with spoon
Stir-fry until pork is no longer pink (5-7 minutes)
Add shredded cabbage and diced carrots
Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until vegetables slightly softened but still have texture
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sesame oil
Stir in green onions
Season with salt and pepper to taste
Remove from heat and let cool to room temperature
Place lumpia wrapper on work surface with corner pointing toward you
Place 2-3 tablespoons filling on lower third of wrapper
Fold bottom corner up over filling, fold in sides, then roll tightly
Seal edge with water if needed
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) for deep frying
Fry lumpia in batches until golden brown and crispy (2-3 minutes)
Drain on paper towels
Serve hot with sweet and sour sauce or vinegar dipping sauce
dinner.notes: Lumpia can be made ahead and reheated. Don't overfill or wrapper will burst during frying
dinner.fun_fact: Lumpia was adapted from Chinese spring rolls during Philippine colonial period but became distinctly Filipino
